stories.title: Meta blocks TikTok ads as its apps push further into full-screen video
paragraphs: Meta said it immediately barred ByteDance advertising on Facebook and Instagram in the United States, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam. The restriction also covers third-party campaigns linking to TikTok and other ByteDance properties in those markets.

Reuters frames the move as an escalation in competition for users, creators, and ad dollars. The Verge separately reports tests that open some users in India directly into full-screen Reels, bringing the apps closer to a video-first layout; Meta says users can still reach the traditional feed.
TikTok and ByteDance had not commented to Reuters when it published. Neither report gives a measure of how many advertisers or users the changes affect.

scoreNotes.general: A concrete competitive move between two major short-video platforms, paired with a visible product test that reinforces the rivalry.
scoreNotes.heat: Meta's restriction reaches seven countries and applies to TikTok and other ByteDance ads; the feature test affects how Facebook and Instagram present video.
scoreNotes.time: Both developments were reported October 8.

paragraphs: The Triple-i Initiative held its first fall presentation on October 8, showing 40 games in roughly 40 minutes without hosts or ad breaks. Coverage described it as the event’s largest batch of new demos and playtests so far.

The announcements ranged from a new Machinarium sequel and an Among Us single-player detective spin-off to same-day demos for games including Hela and Militsioner. Dave the Diver also revealed a Subnautica 2 crossover and reported that the game has passed 10 million copies sold.

stories.title: Creators at an AI conference defend the tools as backlash and job concerns grow
paragraphs: Business Insider reported that hundreds of creators, marketers, brands, and AI advocates attended AI Creator Day, where participants presented work made with generative video, image, and writing tools despite wider backlash against AI content.

Some speakers emphasized human direction and craft, while a panel raised the risk of misleading audiences about what is AI-made. Creator Vincent Marcus, who has more than 1.3 million Instagram followers, said he expects AI could eliminate his voice-acting work and is preparing for that possibility.
The report captures one event rather than a representative survey, and it does not establish how many creators are adopting these tools or how audiences respond to the work.

stories.title: Jagex apologizes after a RuneScape quest trailer shows apparent generative AI art
paragraphs: At RuneFest, a trailer for RuneScape 3's Dragon Slayer 2 quest showed conspicuous image errors, including a character with six fingers. Jagex removed it while investigating after viewers identified apparent generative AI use.

Jagex said its external production partner had assured the studio that it would not use generative AI, apologized for missing the errors, and said it is overhauling its review process. It also plans to commission community creators to tell the quest's story.

This follows a separate AI-related dispute over 100 Thieves RuneScape merchandise. Jagex says it does not knowingly use generative AI for game art or creative assets; the back-to-back partner incidents put its vendor checks under scrutiny.

scoreNotes.general: A second AI-related partner failure led Jagex to acknowledge a review gap and announce a process change.
scoreNotes.heat: The incident followed a separate RuneScape merchandise controversy and drew visible criticism after the RuneFest reveal.

stories.title: Jagex announces a new RuneScape MMO, provisionally called RuneScape 4
paragraphs: Jagex announced a new MMO with the working title RuneScape 4 at its annual RuneFest event. The project began as an expansion to the studio's survival game Dragonwilds before playtesters asked for a more traditional MMO set in that world.

The early teaser points to a fantasy setting connected to Dragonwilds, while the report says the new game is being built in Unreal Engine. Jagex has not announced a release date, and turning an expansion into a standalone MMO likely extends the original 2027 target.

RuneScape 4 would join RuneScape 3 and Old School RuneScape, giving Jagex another major product to develop alongside its established games. The available announcement leaves its relationship to those live communities unresolved.

paragraphs: PC Gamer reports that more than 70 Supermassive employees have left after the studio said up to 75 roles were at risk. The latest figures are based on posts from former staff, including a senior employee who listed developers, artists, producers, QA, and operations among those leaving.

At Ninja Theory, employees have reported being let go or entering consultation as Microsoft moves toward closure after sale attempts fell through. The report also describes fear of future cuts among The Coalition workers after Gears of War: E-Day's story director was laid off in September.

The Coalition has announced no layoffs, and concerns there remain employee accounts rather than a confirmed new cut. Together, the reports show how restructuring is affecting teams even around major releases.

stories.title: Jagex removes RuneScape trailer after fans flag apparent AI art
paragraphs: Jagex removed a trailer for RuneScape 3's Dragon Slayer 2 quest while it investigates after viewers flagged apparent generative-AI errors, including a knight with six fingers. The studio said an outside production partner had explicitly assured it that generative AI would not be used, and apologized for missing the problem.

Jagex says this is the second recent AI-related concern involving trusted partners, following the separate 100 Thieves RuneScape merchandise dispute. It acknowledged its review process failed, promised an overhaul after RuneFest, and said it will commission community creators to retell the quest story.
In sampled discussion, players criticized the oversight and the art, while some defended the staff's intentions; the reaction puts pressure on Jagex's stated limits on AI use in creative work.

scoreNotes.general: A fresh controversy touches a major game's creative process, vendor oversight, and the community's trust in Jagex's public AI commitments.

stories.title: Steam is estimated to have set a September spending record
paragraphs: Alinea Analytics estimates Steam generated $1.7 billion in September, 13% above its previous September record. It estimates the third quarter at $5.5 billion and January through September at $16.5 billion.

Among the 500 highest-grossing Steam games, established franchises accounted for 79.5% of September revenue, while new intellectual property released in 2026 contributed 20.5%. The mix points to the continued weight of familiar catalogs alongside a busy new-release market.
These are analyst estimates rather than figures published by Valve. Alinea says the pace could put Steam above $20 billion for the year, but that remains a projection.

scoreNotes.general: A large market signal with useful detail about what is driving spending, tempered by the fact that Valve does not disclose these revenue figures.
scoreNotes.heat: The estimated $1.7 billion month and record quarter are platform-wide signals relevant to developers, publishers, and investors.
scoreNotes.time: The September estimate was reported October 3, within the seven-day fallback window.
scoreNotes.ethos: Tom's Hardware attributes the estimates to Alinea Analytics; Steam has not confirmed revenue figures, so these remain analyst estimates.

stories.title: Wardogs passes an estimated $100 million in Steam sales
paragraphs: Market analyst Alinea Analytics estimates Wardogs has grossed more than $100 million on Steam and sold 3.2 million copies, including preorders. Its estimate for September alone was $86.9 million after the September 10 early-access launch.
Alinea puts the game at about 250,000 players a day. GamesRadar notes that its comparable early launch revenue remained below Arc Raiders and Helldivers 2, despite Wardogs' strong start.

This adds current sales and audience estimates to Owl's earlier report of three million copies sold. The numbers signal launch reach, but do not establish whether the live-service shooter will retain players over time.

stories.title: Meta tests prompt-based tools for building games across its platforms
paragraphs: Meta introduced Horizon Create, a mobile app, and Horizon Studio, a browser workspace, for making and editing 2D and 3D games with text prompts. Studio also adds visual editing and controls for adjusting assets and game behavior.

Games published through either tool become eligible for native distribution across Facebook, Instagram, and Horizon. Meta describes this as a path from seeing a game in a feed to playing it, but reports no creator adoption or player numbers yet.

Both products are still being tested with Meta's creator community, with wider access planned through a waitlist. The approach brings game-making, distribution, discovery, and future monetization under one platform owner.

stories.title: Riot says 2XKO needed hundreds of thousands of daily players to survive
paragraphs: Riot Games chief product officer Marc Merrill said 2XKO would have needed at least hundreds of thousands of daily players to justify continued support. At the game's cost structure, he said, the requirement could have reached the high hundreds of thousands or millions.

The free-to-play 2v2 fighter is based on League of Legends characters. Riot had already said active development would end in December, citing retention, engagement, and other performance factors; Merrill also pointed to strategy disagreements inside the company.
The estimate underscores the scale of audience pressure behind a live-service game, but Riot did not release 2XKO's actual player count.

scoreNotes.general: A rare concrete look at the scale of audience a live-service fighting game needed to sustain ongoing support.
scoreNotes.heat: The number puts the economics behind Riot's recently announced shutdown in sharp relief, although it is an executive's estimate rather than a disclosed internal target document.
scoreNotes.time: Riot's product chief gave the explanation in an October 2 report, weeks after the planned end of active development was announced.
scoreNotes.ethos: Shacknews reports Marc Merrill's remarks on a podcast and provides the closure context; the audience threshold is attributed to him, not independently audited.

citations.title: 2XKO needed 'hundreds of thousands' of daily active users to survive, says Riot Games CPO

stories.title: Krafton cancels PUBG extraction shooter Black Budget
paragraphs: Krafton and PUBG Corporation have ended development of PUBG: Black Budget, an extraction-shooter spinoff announced in late 2025. The decision followed several closed alpha tests.

The developers said the project's current direction would not produce an experience players could enjoy over the long term. The game had been quiet since June, when its team said playtest participation and feedback were going well.
The cancellation removes another planned entrant from the extraction-shooter field; the developers did not give more detail about what changed or report test numbers.

scoreNotes.general: A clear cancellation of a major publisher's attempt to extend a globally known game brand into a crowded genre.
scoreNotes.heat: PUBG is a major franchise and the project had undergone multiple closed tests, though no current audience or commercial data was reported.
scoreNotes.time: The cancellation was reported October 2 after the project had gone quiet since June.
scoreNotes.ethos: The studio's stated reason is quoted from its Steam developer post in Shacknews' report; no independent explanation of the decision is available.

citations.title: PUBG: Black Budget extraction shooter spinoff canceled
